title: Derived global sections of a derived direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. For every open subscheme $U\subseteq Y$, with $f_U:f^{-1}U\to U$ and exact restriction $E|_{f^{-1}U}$ [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps], there is a natural isomorphism $R\Gamma(U,R(f_U)_*(E|_{f^{-1}U}))\cong R\Gamma(f^{-1}U,E|_{f^{-1}U})$ in the unbounded derived category of abelian groups; $R(f_U)_*$ is the derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] and $R\Gamma$ is the derived global-sections functor [def-pc-open-module-derived-sections].

proof.text: Put V=f^{-1}U and g=f_U. Let F be module direct image along g, G be abelian-group sections on U, and H be abelian-group sections on V. The identity H=F followed by G is definitional: inverse image preserves the top open and forgetting the scalar restriction leaves the underlying abelian group unchanged.

Apply isIso_directImage_globalSections_unit_on_kInjective to g and any K-injective complex I on V. This gives invertibility of the module-valued global-sections unit at F(I). Choose the standard derived category for modules over Gamma(U,O_U), an auxiliary category only. Forgetting these modules to abelian groups is exact. The composite right-derived unit is therefore invertible, using isRightDerivedFunctor_rightDerivedFunctor_comp_of_exact and its descent factorization; cancel its invertible descent comparison. Since module-valued global sections followed by forgetting is definitionally G, the G unit at F(I) is invertible.

Form rightDerivedFunctorCompUnit F G. On a K-injective complex its factors are the invertible G unit from Step 2 and G applied to the invertible F unit. The K-injective localizer criterion makes RF followed by RG a right derived functor of F followed by G. Right-derived uniqueness gives RF followed by RG isomorphic to RH. Whisker this natural isomorphism by the derived exact restriction from X to V, obtaining exactly the stated functor isomorphism with all four localization universes independent.
